questions.question: The normal chromosome complement in males is
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• A normal Human has 23 pairs of chromosomes (46 chromosomes) out of which 22 pairs are autosomes or allosomes (Non - sex chromosomes), while the 23rd pair is the sex chromosome which is responsible for the hereditary changes.
 
• The **normal chromosome complement in human males is** **46XY** i.e. 46 chromosomes including 1X & 1Y chromosomes.
 
• These **X **&** Y** chromosomes form the **sex pair of chromosomes**
 
• The normal chromosome complement in human females is 46XX i.e. 46 chromosomes including 2X chromosomes.
 
• These **2X** chromosomes form the sex pair of chromosomes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fce5bef13942ed80bd9ec28e3af809626bbfb7f9a3f7f72bab9067a34f2fa0db.png]

• Any deviation from this normal arrangement of chromosomes may result in a disorder or syndrome.
 
• These disorders may arise either by addition, deletion, or nonfunctioning of a single or multiple chromosomes.
 
• Examples of such disorders are Turner syndrome, Edward's syndrome, Patau's syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome, etc.

questions.question: Vacuoles are present mainly of large size in _______

options.text: both plant cells and animal cells

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**plant cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles found in cells.
 
• They are primarily present in **plant cells** and are usually large and central.
 
• The main function of vacuoles in plant cells is to maintain **turgor pressure**, which keeps the plant rigid and upright.
 
• Vacuoles store **nutrients, waste products, and other substances** essential for the cell's survival.
 
• In plant cells, the vacuole can occupy up to **90% of the cell's volume**.
 
• The membrane that surrounds a vacuole is called the **tonoplast**.
 
• Vacuoles also play a role in **cell growth** by absorbing water and enlarging, which helps the cell to expand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bacteria**__

 __
 
• **Bacteria** are prokaryotic microorganisms that do not have membrane-bound organelles such as vacuoles.
 
• They have simpler structures compared to eukaryotic cells and rely on other mechanisms for storage and waste management.
 
 
 
• **Both plant cells and animal cells**__
 __
 
• While **both plant and animal cells** have vacuoles, they are more prominent and larger in plant cells.
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are smaller and more numerous, serving different functions such as storage and transport.
 
 
 
• **Animal cells**__
 
 
• **Animal cells** do have vacuoles, but they are typically smaller and serve different roles compared to those in plant cells.
 
• Animal cell vacuoles are involved in processes like **sequestering waste products** and **helping in intracellular digestion**.

questions.question: A DNA has 4000 base pairs. How many turns or helices will be there in that DNA?
questions.solution:
**__Concept__****-**

__
 
• DNA **(****Deoxyribonucleic acid), the genetic material** of living organisms was first discovered by **F. Meischer.**
 
• **Watson** and **Crick** proposed a **double helix model of DNA**.
 
• It consists of **two complementary strands** that run antiparallel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d59a72c51201c870ddae05571fda531c8b14b0b1bfb3cd25b373069ad573b4cb.png] 

**Explanation__**-

__
 
• DNA has roughly **10 bp in each turn.**

 
 
• 10bp = 1turn
 
• 1bp = 1/10 turn
 
• 4000 bp = 1/10x4000 = 400bp
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments(regarding bacteriophages) of **Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase.**

questions.question: 'The daughter cells have the same number of chromosomes as mother cell.' This happens in _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mitosis**__.

 __**Explanation-**__

**Mitosis-**

__
 
• This is the most dramatic period of cell cycle.
 
• Mitosis is the **division of a parent cell into two identical daughter cells**, each with a nucleus having the same amount of DNA, **the same number and kind of chromosomes**, and the same heredity as the parent cell. Therefore, it is also known as** equivalent division**.
 
• That is, the **chromosome number in daughter cells **(progeny) and **mother cell** (parental) **becomes the same**.
 
• Mitosis is divided into the following four stages-
 
 
• **Prophase- **
 
 
• This phase is known for the **initiation of condensation of chromosomal material**.
 
• In this chromatin condensation becomes untangled and finally the centriole begins to move towards the opposite poles of the animal cell.
 
 
 
• **Metaphase-**
 
 
• The **chromosomes spread out** through the cytoplasm of the cell and are seem to be the shortest and thickest.
 
 
 
• **Anaphase- **
 
 
• It is known to be the **shortest duration phase**.
 
• At the beginning of this phase, the **splitting of chromosomes takes place**.
 
 
 
• **Telophase-**
 
 
• This is considered to be a **long and complex phase**.
 
• In this phase, the **spindle fibers disappear**.
 
 
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Meiosis-**

 
• Meiosis is the phenomenon that occurs in any life cycle that **involves the process of sexual reproduction**.
 
• The production of offspring by sexual reproduction involves the fusion of two gametes.
 
• Thus, meiosis is known to be the **specialized form of cell division** that **reduces the chromosome number** in such a way that each daughter nuclei receive only one set of each kind of chromosome (i.e., maternal and paternal).

questions.question: Which of the following does not occur within mitochondria ?
questions.solution:
__**Concept**__-

__
 
• **Mitochondria **is is a double-layered cell organelle, in which the outer layer is porous and the inner layer is folded upon itself is known to be cristae.
 
• The number of **mitochondria **in a single cell may be up to 50 to 5000.
 
• The inner lumen of **mitochondria **contains ribosome phosphate particles and DNA molecules.
 
• It has the potential to synthesize its own protein and oxidation of carbohydrates and fats are taken place with the help of enzymes in **mitochondria**.
 
• This energy is stored in the form of ATP ( Adenosine Triphosphate ) so, these are known as the** "Powerhouse of the cell".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 **Glycolysis does not occur within mitochondria.**

__
 
• The term **glycolysis **has originated from the Greek words,** glycos for sugar, and lysis for splitting.**
 
• The scheme of glycolysis was given by Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof, and J. Parnas, and is often referred to as the EMP pathway.
 
• In anaerobic organisms, it is the only process in **respiration**.
 
• **Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of the cell **and is present in all living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Krebs cycle**

 
• The TCA cycle commonly known as Kreb's cycle occurs in the matrix of mitochondria.
 
• All the enzymes of the TCA cycle or Krebs cycle are present in the matrix of mitochondria except marker enzyme succinic dehydrogenase.

**ATP synthesis**

 
• The number of ATP molecules synthesized depends on the nature of the electron donor.
 
• Oxidation of one molecule of NADH gives rise to 3 molecules of ATP, while that of one molecule of FADH2 produces 2 molecules of ATP.

**Electron transport chain**

 
• The metabolic pathway through which the electron passes from one carrier to another is called the electron transport system (ETS).
 
• It is present in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.question: During cell division, DNA synthesis takes place in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interphase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **DNA or deoxyribonucleic acid **is a group of molecules, responsible for carrying and transferring hereditary traits or genetic information from parents to their offspring.
 
• **Almost every cell** of a **multicellular organism contains the complete set of DNA** required for that organism.
 
• **The Synthesis phase(S phase) of a cell cycle occurs during interphase**, before mitosis or meiosis.
 
• It is responsible for the **synthesis as well as the replication of DNA**.
 
• The **genetic material of a cell is being doubled before** it enters mitosis or meiosis which is **allowing it to split DNA into daughter cells**.
 
• Interphase is the resting phase between successive mitotic divisions of a cell, or between the first and second divisions of meiosis.
 
• Interphase is the longest stage in the eukaryote cell cycle. During interphase, the cell acquires nutrients, creates and uses proteins and other molecules, and starts the process of cell division by replicating the DNA. Interphase is divided into three distinct stages, Gap 1, Synthesis, and Gap 2.
 
• During interphase, the **cell's DNA is not condensed or properly packed**.
 
• It is loosely distributed.
 
• This **stain also represents the organization of the aligned structure** of the chromosomes during the mitosis process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaphase**- During **anaphase, each pair of chromosomes are separated** into two **identical, independent chromosom**es.

 
 
• The chromosomes may be separated by a **structure called the mitotic spindle**.
 
 
 
• **Prophase**- This is the** first phase of mitosis. Identification and separation** of the duplicated genetic material are carried in the nucleus.
 
• **Telophase**- During telophase, the **newly separated chromosomes reach the mitotic spindle**, and a nuclear membrane forms around each set of chromosomes, **thus creating two separate nuclei inside the same cell**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3efaad64d7e336316c9fb316ece0775472d6271c57b38d9a9788331a014f15e.png]

questions.question: Which of the following are found in prokaryotic cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Prokaryotic cells are primitive cells, i.e. they lack a true membrane-bound nucleus.
 
• Most of the prokaryotes are bacteria.
 
• Prokaryotic genetic material lies naked in the cytoplasm, and replication of DNA occurs in the cytoplasm only.
 
• **Ribosomes are found in prokaryotic cells.**
 
• Several prokaryotic bacterial cells like Nostoc, Anabaena are capable of nitrogen fixation, they can fix atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.
 
• Autotrophic prokaryotes synthesize organic molecules from inorganic molecules of carbon dioxide.
 
• Plasmids are double-stranded, closed circular, symbiotic DNA molecules that occur naturally in bacteria (prokaryote), outside the bacterial chromosome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The mitochondrion** is a membrane-bound structure with outer and inner membranes.

 
 
• Mitochondria are said to be the sites of aerobic respiration.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called **‘power houses’ of the cell. **
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles.
 
 
• It is present in both plant and animal cells. 
 
• Vacuoles are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents. It is also used to store food for the cell. 
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes **are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the Golgi apparatus.
 
 
• These are also called '**'Suicidal bags'**' because of their phagocytic activity.

questions.question: The process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography (habitats) is called ______.
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**adaptive radiation**__. • **Adaptive radiation (divergent evolution)** is the evolution from one species of animals or plants of many different forms. • The original population **increases in size** and it spreads out from its center of origin to exploit new habitats and food sources. • This results in many populations each adapted to its particular habitat. Eventually, these populations will differ from each other **sufficiently to become new species**.

questions.question: What is Gene therapy?

options.text: Method to replace a defective gene with a healthy gene
Method aim to cure genetic disorders
Method to provide correct version of the defective gene

questions.solution:
The correct answer __**All of the above**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gene therapy** is a **technique **that uses genes to treat or prevent disease. 
 
• Researchers are testing several approaches to gene therapy, like -

 
• **Replacing a mutated gene that causes disease with a healthy gene.**
 
• **Inactivating, a mutated gene that is functioning not properly.**
 
• **Introducing a new gene into the body to help fight a disease.**

 
• Although gene therapy is a promising treatment option for a number of diseases (including inherited disorders, some types of cancer, and certain viral infections).
 
• Gene therapy is currently being tested only for diseases that have no other option for cures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are **two different types **of gene therapy -

 
• **Somatic gene therapy -**

 
• It involves the insertion of a common and** healthy gene into the appropriate cells **of an individual that is affected by a genetic disease,
 
• This technique cures the disorder permanently. The gene is carried in the person's cell by the virus.

 
• **Germline gene therapy -**

 
• When the drug-gene is introduced into a **germ cell or zygote**, it is called germline gene therapy.
 
• Changes in somatic gene therapy are not modifiable, whereas germline gene therapies are modifiable.

questions.question: The term ‘Founder effect’, in population genetics, is used to indicate?

options.text: reduced genetic variation as compared to the original population
increased genetic variation as compared to the original population
confinement of successive generations in the geographical area that is the original habitat of the founders.
retreat of successive generations from the geographical area that is the original habitat of the founders.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1 only__.

__
 
• **The term ‘Founder effect’, in population genetics, is used to indicate reduced genetic variation as compared to the original population.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The term "founder effect" refers** to the observation when a small group of individuals breaks off from a larger population and** establishes a new population**.

 
 
• The particular alleles may not be representative of the larger population.
 
• As the new population grows, the allele frequencies will usually **continue to reflect the original small group**.
 
 
 
• A **founder effect occurs when a new colony** is started by a few members of the original population.
 
• This small population size means that the colony may have:
 
 
• **reduced genetic variation from the original population**.
 
• **a non-random sample of the genes in the original population**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70c66fc6aa2a5a4d365ae07e925d7fb22ea04b19e119e2ec712c03ebed8b00ee.png] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• A** population bottleneck or genetic bottleneck** is a sharp reduction in the size of a population.

 
 
• It is due to environmental events such as famines, earthquakes, floods, fires, disease, and droughts or human activities such as genocide and human population planning.
 
• The frequency of certain **alleles in a population change** because the organisms that carry them are eliminated.
 
• The others increase in number because they are the only alleles left.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, the quality of a cell to regenerate and grow into a new braird or plant is known as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Totipotency**__.

__
 
• **Totipotency is the ability of a single cell to divide and produce all of the differentiated cells in an organism.**__

 __
 
• Spores and zygotes are examples of totipotent cells.
 
• In the spectrum of cell potency, totipotency represents the cell with the greatest differentiation potential.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Many somatic plant cells**, including some fully differentiated types (e.g. leaf mesophyll), provided they contain intact nuclear, plastid, and mitochondrial genomes, have the capacity to regenerate into whole plants.
 
• This phenomenon is **totipotency**, amazing developmental plasticity that sets plant cells apart from most of their animal counterparts, and was ﬁrst demonstrated by **Steward and Reinert** in the 1950s.

questions.question: The proteins and lipids which are essential for building the cell membrane are manufactured by
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The endoplasmic reticulum is a part of the **endomembrane system**.
 
• These are tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm and consist of membrane-bound channels, tubules, sacs, or vesicles.
 
• On the basis of the presence of ribosomes ER of two types **rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum**.
 
• If ribosomes are attached to the endoplasmic reticulum then it is called a **rough endoplasmic reticulum** and if there are no ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum then it is called a **smooth endoplasmic reticulum**.

**Explanation:__**

__
 
• The proteins and lipids which are essential for building the cell membrane are manufactured in the **Endoplasmic reticulum (ER).**
 
• **Rough ER **is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in **protein synthesis **and secretion.
 
• The **Smooth ER **is the major site for the synthesis of lipids.
 
• In animal cells, lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesized in **SER**.
 
• **ER **also** **acts as an internal support for cytoplasm.
 
• Plasma membrane lipids and proteins are synthesized by the endoplasmic reticulum through the process known as **membrane biosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce8bc14d916bae4bfdae4fa49ba546548f28a8381f7c554d094c6a0602c61ba2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Mitochondria:**

 
• These are sausage-shaped, cylindrical double membrane-bound cell organelles.
 
• Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration.
 
• They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, thus they are called the "powerhouse of the cell".
 
• The mitochondrial matrix contains circular DNA, 70S ribosomes, and enzymes that take part in protein synthesis and respiration respectively.

**Plasma membrane:**

 
• It is a selectively permeable outer layer of the cell.
 
• PM is composed of lipids that are arranged in a bilayer.
 
• The important functions of PM include the transport of materials, mechanical barrier, cell division, formation of intercellular junctions, osmosis, endocytosis, and secretion, and it also ensures cellular integrity.

**Golgi apparatus:**

 
• Golgi apparatus are membrane-bound cell organelles with flat or disc-shaped sacs, tubules, and vesicles. 
 
• Its important functions include the storage, modification, and packaging of biochemical compounds.
 
• It is also the major site of the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

**Hence, the correct answer is Endoplasmic reticulum.**

questions.question: Cell wall is not found in
questions.solution:
Cell: 

__
 
• The cell is the fundamental unit of life. All the life activities are carried out by cells.
 
• The organisms are classified based on the number of cells present in them.
 
• Unicellular organisms are single-celled, while multicellular organisms have a large number of cells. 
 
• Plants have both a cell wall and a cell membrane (plasma membrane). 
 
• ​The cell wall is present in Plant cells while it is absent in animal cells. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The cell wall is the outer covering of a cell.
 
• It surrounds the plasma membrane of plant cells and provides tensile strength and protection against mechanical and osmotic stress.
 
• The cell wall is present in plant, bacterial and fungal cells and absent in animal cells.
 
• The plasma membrane (also called the cell membrane) is the membrane found in all cells that separate the interior of the cell from the outside environment.
 
• In bacterial and plant cells, a cell wall is attached to the plasma membrane on its outside surface.
 
• The plasma membrane is present in both plant cells and animal cells.
 
• The plant cell wall is mainly composed of cellulose.
 
• The plasma membrane or the cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids and proteins.
 
• The major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged in a bilayer.

**Thus, a cell wall is not found in an animal cell.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bc71d9937632a668e6c99f27b84a373f0fe7b01138a3d63d7e073a2cf85dc2b.png]

questions.question: After protein synthesis by ribosomes, the newly synthesized proteins are assisted in their folding and transport by special proteins called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chaperone.

__Concept:__

Endoplasmic reticulum (ER): 

__
 
• ER is a network of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm.
 
• ER serves as a channel for the transport of materials between the various region of the cytoplasm or between cytoplasm and nucleus.
 
• ER often shows ribosomes on their outer surface.
 
• There are 2 types of ER:** Rough endoplasmic reticulum **(RER) and **Smooth endoplasmic reticulum **(SER).
 
• ER-bearing ribosomes on their surface are called **RER** and are involved in protein synthesis and secretion.
 
• In the absence of ribosomes, the surface appears smooth and called **SER** and is the major site for the synthesis of** lipid.**

**Explanation:**__

**Chaperones: **They are a functionally related group of proteins assisting protein folding in cells under physiological and stress conditions.

__
 
• The newly synthesized proteins are assisted in their folding by special proteins called chaperones or chaperone proteins.
 
• These proteins help to ensure that the proteins fold into their proper three-dimensional structure, which is necessary for their function. In addition, they also assist in avoiding mistakes in the folding process that could lead to aggregation or misfolding of proteins.
 
• For transporting proteins to their appropriate locations within or outside the cell, there are various mechanisms in place. One of the commonly known transport systems involves proteins called vesicle coat proteins (like COPI and COPII), which help package proteins in vesicles and transport them between different parts of the cell.

So, the correct answer is **Chaperone.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dystrophin:** In skeletal cardiac muscles, dystrophin is a group of proteins that work together to strengthen muscle fibers and protect them from injury as muscles contract and relax. It has 2 subunits - α and β
 
• **Coronin: **It is an actin-binding protein that also interacts with microtubules and also in some cell types is associated with phagocytes.

 

**Ribophorin:** Ribosomes are the sites for protein synthesis so they are called the protein factory of the cells.

 
• Ribophorin's role is different from that of chaperones. Ribophorins are part of the translocon complex involved in the translocation of newly synthesized proteins into the ER.
 
• Ribophorin are ribosome receptor proteins that aid in the binding of the 60s subunit of eukaryotic ribosomes to the RER.
 
• There are 2 types of ribophorin- Ribophorin I and Ribophorin II.
 
• Ribophorins I and II, a transmembrane glycoprotein of the rough endoplasmic reticulum, intervene in the union of the ribosomes to the Rough Endoplasmic membrane.
 
• They play an important role in the co-translational translocation process which depends on this union.

questions.question: Protein synthesis takes place on the surface of:
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Protein synthesis is a process of production of proteins required for the cells of any living organism. Proteins are biomolecules needed by our body for the growth and multiplication of cells. 
 
• Proteins are also known as building blocks of life. Proteins perform numerous functions in our body. Some proteins are a part of the structure of cells, those are called **Structural proteins.**
 
• Some proteins act as** Enzymes **which are biological catalysts or **bio-catalysts.** These enzymes speed up the rate of a reaction without taking part in the reaction. Some proteins act as **Hormones **That regulate the functioning of our body. 
 
• These proteins are made up of many smaller subunits which are called **amino acids.** These amino acids are monomers that join with each other in a specific sequence to form a polymer (bigger molecule) of protein.
 
• Amino acids are synthesized inside the cells, Thus the process of formation of proteins is also known as Bio-synthesis of proteins or Protein synthesis.
 
• Protein synthesis is a process that initiates inside the nucleus and completes in the cytoplasm on the surface of the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• The process of protein synthesis includes **Transcription** and **Translation. **

 
• Transcription: It is the process of **copying genetic information** from one strand of DNA to single-stranded mRNA. During this process synthesis of a complementary RNA, strand takes place.
 
• Translation: Translation is the mechanism in which coded information is translated & specific amino acids are prepared which forms a polypeptide on ribosomes.

 
• The process of protein synthesis is very important for every living organism. Any change or problem in protein synthesis causes severe physiological disorders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3620dd6e32f44c97b031cfcb54a35e4c289de6a77091d7edcc599d6c392fc0f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Different cell organelles perform different functions in our body.
 
• **Nucleus**: The Nucleus is an important cell organelle that contains and controls the genetic material of the cell. As the nucleus has entire genetic information of the cell, it also plays an important role in **heredity and variation**. It is the characteristic cell organelle in Eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum**: It is a little network that connects the nucleus & the cytoplasm. If the Endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to it, it is called a rough endoplasmic reticulum. If the endoplasmic reticulum lacks ribosomes, it is known as Smooth endoplasmic reticulum. Smooth ER is involved in various processes like a synthesis of lipids, detoxification of drugs & poisons, storage of calcium ions, etc.
 
• **Chloroplast**: The chloroplasts are plastids which contain a green coloured pigment known as Chlorophyll. Chloroplasts are present in plant cells. It is the active site for photosynthesis.

questions.question: For protein synthesis, the amino acids are recognized and carried by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**Transfer RNA:**

 
• **Protein synthesis** involves translating the genetic information stored within the DNA into functional proteins. This process takes place in two major steps: **transcription and translation.**
 
• **Transcription** is the first step where a copy of the gene's sequence (a sequence in the DNA) is made into a molecule called messenger RNA (mRNA).
 
• **Translation** is the process in which the information in mRNA (brought from the DNA) is read by molecular machinery called the ribosome to synthesize a protein.
 
• **tRNA plays a pivotal role in translation**. Each tRNA molecule has an** anti-codon sequence **that** corresponds to a particular mRNA codon** (a sequence of three nucleotides on the mRNA that corresponds to a specific amino acid).
 
• **When tRNA recognizes and pairs with its corresponding mRNA codon **in the ribosome, **the amino acid it carries gets added to the growing peptide chain, forming the protein**.
 
• Thus, in protein synthesis, **tRNA recognizes and carries specific amino acids according to the genetic code for the assembly of proteins.**
 
• **Hence the correct answer is option 4**

questions.question: In DNA, thymine always pairs with ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer __**Adenine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are **four nitrogen bases** in a DNA-

 
 
• Adenine
 
• Guanine
 
• Thymine
 
• Cytosine
 
 
 
• **Adenine **pairs with up **Thymine**
 
• **Guanine **pairs up with **Cytosine**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• DNA stands for **Deoxyribo Nucleic Acid**.
 
• It contains genetic information.
 
• **It is made up of**
 
 
• sugar group - deoxyribose sugar
 
• phosphate group
 
• nitrogen base - (Adenine, Guanine, Thymine, Cytosine)
 
 
 
• Genetic information in DNA is wrapped up around a protein called **Histones**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **RNA** (RiboNucleic Acid) also has 4 nitrogenous base.

 
 
• Adenine
 
• Guanine
 
• Cytosine
 
• Uracil (instead of Thymine which is present in DNA)
 
 
 
• RNA is **single-stranded biopolymer**. 
 
• **It is of 3 types**-
 
 
• mRNA (messenger)
 
• tRNA (transfer)
 
• rRNA (ribosomal)
